sentences.text: Charlotte Brontë and her sisters bet their savings on the hottest tech stock of the eighteen forties.
This week, people are asking if AI stocks are a bubble.
Back then, the hot tech was trains.
You see, Emily Brontë ran the family money, and she bought into the Railway King, George Hudson.
Their fifty-pound shares shot up to a hundred and twenty, and their income nearly tripled.
Her sisters said no, so she stayed in with them.
So how was the Railway King paying everyone?
With the money new shareholders had just put in.
Then the bubble popped, and the shares fell to twenty.
Some say Charlotte's money from Jane Eyre went down with them.
One sister saw it coming. Two didn't.
